first.rationale: Competitive entry pricing creates an immediate acquisition risk among price-sensitive SMBs, and prior evidence indicates targeted promotional pricing can lift both acquisition and revenue. A guarded segment-specific test is preferable to a broad discount because discounting may attract lower-quality demand or reduce long-term realized value. Onboarding deterioration is also material, so memory_86 is requested to compare whether its adoption benefit plausibly outweighs the immediate competitive revenue threat before commitment.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening the self-serve onboarding flow. Onboarding completion is currently down 4% QoQ, and the verified prior experiment increased completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%, supporting sustainable qualified revenue rather than only top-of-funnel volume. Do not use promotional pricing: although it increased acquisition and qualified revenue initially, the verified cohort had 30-day retention decline of 12% and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Guard against reduced qualification or downstream account quality by measuring meaningful activation, qualified conversion, retention, and realized revenue alongside completion.
